mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly defines the work done by a constant force on an object?

options.A: Work is the product of the component of the force along the displacement and the magnitude of the displacement (W = F s cosθ).
options.B: Power is the rate at which work is done.
options.C: Energy is the capacity to do work.
options.D: Force is a push or pull acting on an object.

mcqs.answer: Work is the product of the component of the force along the displacement and the magnitude of the displacement (W = F s cosθ).
mcqs.explanation: The definition of work involves a force component acting in the direction of displacement and the distance moved, expressed as W = F s cosθ. Options B, C and D describe related but distinct concepts, so they are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: A constant force of 10 N is applied at an angle of 60° to the direction of displacement of an object that moves 5 m. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work = F s cosθ = 10 N × 5 m × cos60° = 50 × 0.5 = 25 J. Option B ignores the cosine factor, C would be correct only if the force were perpendicular, and D uses an incorrect angle value.

mcqs.question: In which of the following situations is the work done by the applied force positive?

options.A: A person pushes a box forward in the same direction the box moves.
options.B: A person pulls a sled backward while it slides forward.
options.C: A person holds a weight stationary on a table.
options.D: A person pushes a wall that does not move.

mcqs.answer: A person pushes a box forward in the same direction the box moves.
mcqs.explanation: Positive work occurs when the component of the force is in the same direction as the displacement, as in option A. In B the force is opposite to displacement (negative work), C and D involve no displacement (zero work).

mcqs.question: Which scenario best illustrates negative work being done on an object?

options.A: A car accelerates forward on a straight road.
options.B: A ball is lifted vertically upward against gravity.
options.C: A car slows down because of the frictional force from the road.
options.D: A satellite moves in a circular orbit with no external forces acting.

mcqs.answer: A car slows down because of the frictional force from the road.
mcqs.explanation: Negative work occurs when the force component opposes the direction of displacement. Friction opposing the motion of the car does negative work (option C). Options A and B involve forces in the direction of motion (positive work), while D involves no net external work.

mcqs.question: In which of the following situations is the work done by the applied force zero?

options.A: Carrying a bag of groceries while walking horizontally on a level floor.
options.B: Lifting a book vertically upward onto a shelf.
options.C: Pushing a crate across a rough floor in the direction of the push.
options.D: Pulling a sled up a 30° incline with a rope parallel to the incline.

mcqs.answer: Carrying a bag of groceries while walking horizontally on a level floor.
mcqs.explanation: The force you exert on the bag is upward (to support its weight) while the displacement is horizontal; the angle between force and displacement is 90°, making cosθ = 0, so work = 0. Options B, C, and D involve a component of force along displacement, giving non‑zero work.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand work as a scalar quantity
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly reflects the scalar nature of work?

options.A: Work has magnitude but no direction.
options.B: Work is a vector and follows vector addition rules.
options.C: Work can be represented by an arrow indicating its direction.
options.D: Work changes sign only because the force changes direction, not because of displacement.

mcqs.answer: Work has magnitude but no direction.
mcqs.explanation: Work is defined as a scalar quantity; it is fully described by its magnitude (in joules) and does not possess a direction. Options B and C incorrectly treat work as a vector, and D misstates the reason for sign change, which actually depends on the relative direction of force and displacement.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares work and energy?

options.A: Work is the transfer of energy from one system to another.
options.B: Energy is the rate at which work is performed.
options.C: Both work and energy are vector quantities.
options.D: Work is measured in newtons, whereas energy is measured in joules.

mcqs.answer: Work is the transfer of energy from one system to another.
mcqs.explanation: Work represents the process of transferring energy; when work is done on a system, its energy changes. Option B confuses work with power, C incorrectly labels them as vectors, and D swaps the correct units (work and energy are both measured in joules).

mcqs.learning_point: Use W = F s cos θ
mcqs.question: A constant force of 20 N acts on a particle that moves 8 m. The force makes an angle of 30° with the direction of motion. What is the work done by the force?
mcqs.explanation: Work = F s cosθ = 20 N × 8 m × cos30° = 160 N·m × 0.866 ≈ 138.6 J. Option A ignores the cosine factor, C uses half the force, and D would be correct only for a 90° angle.
